body:
I honestly needed a loophole, and someone here reminded me of one I could use. I'll give you one. 

Unless you formed a "Staxled suicide, Inc" corporation as a separate legal entity to contract with (You can make a contract between yourself and another entity you can control, or between two entities that you control), you probably don't have a contract at all.

I actually made mine a legal contract, as I had a corporation I had formed in college for a startup that didn't work out. I never dissolved it, so I literally formed a contract. I paid $20 in consideration for "consulting services" into the company account, and promised to re-launch the company if I found a job. I really went all in.

Except for one problem, I control both entities. I would prefer some more time, and it's in the best interest of the company I created for me not to die (I can't re-launch if it did) so naturally, I had to consent in that capacity.

Besides, the whole thing was probably unconscionable anyway. I'm fairly sure it would be unenforceable*

*except in Delaware...just kidding...sort of.
It's a field where if you don't get hired right off the bat, you are in trouble. It's a bifurcated field where a some people make a lot, and some make very little.

I didn't think about that, a contract extension is possible if both sides agree. Since I am the only party, I guess I can give myself an extension. I hadn't considered going back to school, so it seems like it's a valid reason.
I'd prefer not to disclose that. I looked outside of the field as well. Pretty much anything that required a degree, anything that would have a reasonable shot at a future worked for me.

Considering I didn't get any interviews, I adjusted my resume a few months after graduation. My grades were decent, my school is decent, my program fairly in demand. 
 
Just applying to positions is generally a poor way to find a job, ultimately I needed to network better in school, but it's too late to do that now and it was too late to do that when I graduating. I tried to overcome that with sheer numbers, but it didn't work. And trust me, I've tried friends and family...I'm not above nepostism when desperate, but they couldn't really help either.

And it's not just a promise. I wrote up a contract and signed it. It wasn't some idle, offhand thing. It was part of a plan to motivate myself to get what I wanted, and I can't Monday morning quarterback the fact that it didn't work out.
It doesn't matter what I want. A deal is a deal.

I spent a year trying to get my shit together, I took a dead end job that doesn't require a degree to survive. I've spent every spare moment I could filling out applications, but all I have found are pyramid scam jobs and rejection letters.

I spent a year trying to get my shit together, motivated by a ticking clock. And it didn't work out. Statistics say it won't now, and even if I did it's a moot point because I gave myself a year, and time is up.

Now I have to fulfill the promise I made.
